targets.claim: Deposit spend cannot consume withdrawal-reserved ETH.
Router-pulled wei equals 32 ETH times actual deposits and leaves no router residual.
Total modeled allocated deposits is the sum of per-module allocated deposits over the finite router module array.
Successful modeled deposit transitions preserve router ETH balance.
Successful nonzero modeled deposit transitions add exactly the pulled value to the beacon sink.
Successful nonzero modeled deposit transitions reduce buffered ETH by exactly the pulled value.
Successful nonzero modeled deposit transitions require the pulled value to be available as depositable ETH before the modeled Lido buffer pull.
Successful zero-deposit transitions do not change modeled buffered ETH or the beacon sink.
Successful modeled deposit transitions leave withdrawal-reserved ETH unchanged.
Successful modeled deposit transitions require an existing active module, nonzero computed capacity, and actual deposits not exceeding that capacity.
Successful modeled deposit transitions update the module array exactly by recording the selected module last-deposit value.
Successful modeled deposit transitions record the selected module last-deposit value as the exact pulled wei amount, including the zero-key return path.
Successful modeled deposit transitions preserve router module-array length while recording last-deposit accounting.
Successful modeled deposit transitions preserve the router module-balance sum while recording last-deposit accounting.
Successful modeled deposit transitions preserve router report accounting: router balance Gwei and the last accepted report.
Successful modeled deposit transitions leave the deposit-reserved ETH bucket unchanged.
Accepted module reports set router validator balance to the module-balance sum.
Successful modeled module-balance report transitions imply Solidity report shape checks: full length, router order, and Gwei range.
Successful modeled module-balance report transitions set router validator balance to the updated module-balance sum.
Successful modeled module-balance report transitions set updated module balances exactly to the accepted report balances.
Successful modeled module-balance report transitions record the exact accepted report for later reward distribution reads.
Successful modeled module-balance report transitions preserve router module-array length.
Successful modeled module-balance report transitions set the module array exactly to the accepted report update loop result.
Successful modeled module-balance report transitions preserve ETH-side state: buffer, reserves, router ETH balance, and beacon sink.
Reward distribution reads the latest accepted module-balance report.
After a successful modeled module-balance report transition, reward distribution reads that accepted report.
Reward fees are bounded by configured basis points and aligned with module recipients.
Reward rows preserve the module id, reward recipient, and computed module reward from the router module array.
Reward distribution rows are produced only from existing nonzero-balance modules and remain aligned with the module recipient.
Every emitted reward distribution row has nonzero validator balance.
A reward distribution row's paid module fee cannot exceed its computed module fee.
Stopped modules have zero paid module fee in the reward distribution row.
Reward distribution returns no rows when the router total validator balance is zero.
Reward distribution returns an empty module-id projection when the router total validator balance is zero.
Reward distribution total fee is exactly the sum of module plus treasury fee over emitted rows.
Non-active or deposit-paused modules receive no deposits.
Stopped modules receive no module reward payment.
Successful modeled exited-count update rows name existing modules, cannot decrease router-stored exited counts, and cannot exceed deposited validators.
An empty modeled exited-count update is a no-op and returns zero newly exited validators.
Successful modeled exited-count updates preserve router module-array length.
Successful modeled exited-count updates preserve the router module-balance sum.
Successful modeled exited-count transitions return exactly the sequential loop result over router modules and input rows.
Successful modeled exited-count updates preserve non-module router state: ETH accounting, router report balance, and last accepted report.
Successful top-up transitions require an active top-up-capable module.
Successful top-up transitions preserve Solidity input shape: nonempty keys with matching node-operator, top-up-limit, and pubkey lengths.
Successful top-up transitions preserve returned allocation checks: same length, Gwei alignment, per-key limits, and rounded module target bound.
Successful top-up transitions keep the returned allocation sum within the module allocation budget.
Successful top-up transitions leave no router ETH residual.
Successful top-up transitions leave router module accounting unchanged.
Successful top-up transitions preserve router report accounting: router balance Gwei and the last accepted report.
Successful nonzero top-up transitions add exactly the allocation sum to the beacon sink.
Successful nonzero top-up transitions reduce buffered ETH by exactly the allocation sum.
Successful top-up transitions leave withdrawal-reserved ETH unchanged.
Successful top-up transitions leave the deposit-reserved ETH bucket unchanged.
Successful nonzero top-up transitions require the allocation sum to be available as depositable ETH before the modeled Lido buffer pull.
Successful zero-sum top-up transitions are no-ops after validation and return the unchanged router state.
Allocation capacity rows stay aligned with router modules.
Allocation capacity arrays preserve router module length.
Allocation capacity value arrays preserve router module length.
Allocation capacity rows preserve router module id order.
Active module capacity is bounded by the module stake-share target.
Active module capacity is bounded by available module capacity.
Inactive module capacity remains equal to current allocation.
Successful reward-minted report transitions require equal module-id and share array lengths.
Successful reward-minted report transitions preserve the Solidity row-validity rule.
Every nonzero reward-minted report row names an existing module.
Zero-share reward-minted rows are skipped before the module-existence check.
Successful reward-minted report transitions return exactly the rows generated by zipping module ids with total shares.
Successful reward-minted report transitions return one generated row per input module id.
Successful reward-minted report transitions preserve module-id order exactly in returned rows.
Successful reward-minted report transitions preserve total-share order exactly in returned rows.
Successful all-module fee updates require module-fee and treasury-fee arrays to match router module length.
Successful all-module fee updates preserve the Solidity consistent-fee-sum validation rule.
Successful all-module fee updates preserve router module-list length.
Successful all-module fee updates set module-fee and treasury-fee projections exactly to the supplied arrays.
After a successful all-module fee update, every updated module fee sum is bounded by total basis points.
Successful all-module fee updates preserve the router module-balance sum.
Successful all-module fee updates preserve non-module router state: ETH accounting, router report balance, and last accepted report.
Successful single-module parameter updates require the selected module to exist.
Successful single-module parameter updates preserve Solidity share, fee-sum, consistency, and uint64-bound validation.
Successful single-module parameter updates preserve router module-list length.
Successful single-module parameter updates record the requested share, fee, max-deposit, and min-distance fields for the selected module.
After a successful single-module parameter update, every updated module fee sum is bounded by total basis points.
Successful single-module parameter updates preserve the router module-balance sum.
Successful single-module parameter updates preserve non-module router state: ETH accounting, router report balance, and last accepted report.

Successful module-status updates record the requested status for the selected module.

Successful add-module transitions require a fresh module id.
Successful add-module transitions preserve share, fee-sum, consistency, and uint64-bound validation.
Successful add-module transitions increase router module-list length by one.
Successful add-module transitions append exactly the module built from the accepted config.
The modeled newly added module starts active with zero accounting fields.
Successful add-module transitions preserve the router module-balance sum.
Successful add-module transitions preserve non-module router state: ETH accounting, router report balance, and last accepted report.
Successful all-module share updates require stake-share and priority-exit arrays to match router module length.
Successful all-module share updates preserve the Solidity share-parameter validation rule for every row.
